newsitem.title: CHINA: HK, U.S. customs to inspect textile factories.
newsitem.headline: HK, U.S. customs to inspect textile factories.

text.p: Hong Kong and United States customs officers will conduct joint visits to Hong Kong garment factories in September as part of an ongoing effort to combat illegal transshipments, the government said on Wednesday.
The teams will observe factory production in 12 categories of textiles and garment products, it said in a statement.
"During the visits, U.S. custom officers will not be involved in any enforcement work such as inspection of factory books and records," it said.
"Any such enforcement activities will be undertaken, if necessary, by Hong Kong Customs independently, and separately from the joint observation visits."
Washington imposed tough import measures against Hong Kong's garment exporters last June to try to stem illegal transshipments from China via Hong Kong to the United States.
Washington says manufacturers in China dodge quota limits by attaching false "Made in Hong Kong" labels.

U.S. customs has since been allowed to join Hong Kong customs officers on visits to the territory's textile factories as part of the local government's effort to detect and prevent illegal transshipments.

Since the crackdown, the United States has announced it will lift a single-entry bond imposed on Hong Kong exporters in eight of 10 categories of garments from May 1 and four other categories of textile products will be removed from a watchlist.
